provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Rights of a child
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list rights of a child.
The pupils should be able to explain why rights are important.
Introduction:
Today we learn about our rights as children.
Rights are things all children should have.
Content:
Rights are what every child needs to be happy and healthy.
Children have right to food.
Children have right to shelter.
Children have right to go to school.
We can say my rights every day.
Class activity:
Let us stand up and say my rights together.
Evaluation questions:
What is a right?
Name one right of a child.
Why do we need rights?
Summary:
Rights help children stay safe and happy.

topics.title: Duties of a child
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state duties of a child.
The pupils should be able to explain why duties are important.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about rights.
Today we learn about duties.
Content:
Duties are what children should do.
We must obey our parents.
We must help at home.
We must do our school work.
Doing duties makes us good children.
Class activity:
Let us act out helping at home.
Evaluation questions:
What is a duty?
Name one duty at home.
Why should we do our school work?
Summary:
Good children do their duties.

topics.title: Working hard
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why hard work pays.
The pupils should be able to tell a story about hard work.
Introduction:
Some people work hard every day.
Hard work helps us get what we want.
Content:
Hard work means trying your best.
Farmers work hard to grow food.
Teachers work hard to teach us.
When we work hard we get good results.
Hard work stories teach us to be strong.
Class activity:
Let us draw a picture of someone working hard.
Evaluation questions:
What is hard work?
Why does hard work pay?
Name one person who works hard.
Summary:
Working hard makes us successful.

topics.title: Money: needs and wants
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between needs and wants.
The pupils should be able to list things we need.
Introduction:\ Money is what we use to buy things.
Some things we need, some we want.
Content:
Needs are things we must have to live.
Food is a need.
Water is a need.
Clothes are a need.
Wants are things we like but don't need.
Toys are wants.
Ice cream is wants.
Class activity:
Let us sort pictures into needs and wants.
Evaluation questions:
What is a need?
What is a want?
Name one thing you need.
Summary:
Needs are important, wants are nice to have.

topics.title: Saving money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we save money.
The pupils should be able to name a way to save money.
Introduction:
Sometimes we have extra money.
We can save money for future.
Content:
Saving means keeping money for later.
We can save money in a kolo.
We can save in a bank.
We save money for important things.
Saving helps us buy big things later.
Class activity:
Let us make paper kolo to save coins.
Evaluation questions:
What is saving?
Why should we save money?
Where can we keep our savings?
Summary:
Saving money helps us prepare for future.

topics.title: Our leaders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify our leaders.
The pupils should be able to explain why we respect leaders.
Introduction:
Nigeria has leaders who help us.
We must respect our leaders.
Content:
The President is our national leader.
Governors lead our states.\ Leaders make rules for us.
We show respect to leaders.
We stand when leaders come.
We listen to leaders.
Class activity:
Let us draw pictures of our leaders.
Evaluation questions:
Who is the President?
Who is your state governor?
Why must we respect leaders?
Summary:
Leaders help our country grow.

topics.title: National symbols
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name national symbols.
The pupils should be able to identify the eagle and coat of arms.
Introduction:
Nigeria has special symbols.
These symbols show our country.
Content:
The eagle is a national symbol.
The eagle is strong and brave.
The coat of arms is a symbol.
The coat of arms has eagle and shield.
National symbols make us proud.
Class activity:
Let us color pictures of national symbols.
Evaluation questions:
Name one national symbol.
What does the eagle represent?
Why do we have national symbols?
Summary:
National symbols show our country's identity.

topics.title: Living in peace
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to live in peace.
The pupils should be able to tell how to settle quarrels.
Introduction:
Peace means no fighting.
We must live in peace with others.
Content:
Sharing helps us live in peace.
Playing well together keeps peace.
When we quarrel we should talk nicely.
We can say sorry to settle quarrels.
Peace makes everyone happy.
Class activity:
Let us practice saying sorry nicely.
Evaluation questions:
What is peace?
How can we share with friends?
What should we do when we quarrel?
Summary:
Peace makes our community nice.

topics.title: Festivals in Nigeria
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name festivals in Nigeria.
The pupils should be able to explain how we celebrate festivals.
Introduction:
Nigeria has many festivals.
Festivals are times for celebration.
Content:
Christmas is a Christian festival.
Sallah is a Muslim festival.
New Yam is an Igbo festival.
We celebrate with food and new clothes.
We visit family during festivals.
Class activity:
Let us draw our favorite festival.
Evaluation questions:
Name one festival in Nigeria.
How do people celebrate Christmas?
What is special about New Yam festival?
Summary:
Festivals bring joy to our communities.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term's work.
The pupils should be able to participate in end of year quiz.
Introduction:
Today we revise what we learned this term.
We will play a quiz to show what we know.
Content:
We learned about rights and duties.
We learned about hard work and money.
We learned about leaders and symbols.
We learned about peace and festivals.
Class activity:
Let us play a quiz game in teams.
Evaluation questions:
What is one right of a child?
Why should we save money?
Name one national symbol.
How do we live in peace?
Summary:
We have learned many important things this year.
